answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because pearl only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, voyage is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any lotus approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
